misconceptions.believed: That three tags -- recursion, regex, numeric -- are carried by exactly one level each and therefore can never reach the confidence threshold from ordinary play. I wrote that in S027's open questions, repeated it in S028's, put it on the flight board, and told the user it was one of two things that would become their call.
misconceptions.revealed_by: Checking it before building W5 on top of it, because W5 was supposed to be its answer. Replaying one level three times banks three observations -- submit observes on every ranked run, not once per level -- so recursion becomes confident on the third replay.
misconceptions.corrected_to: Those tags can become confident. What they cannot do is be measured across more than one problem shape, so the estimate reads 'are you good at w3-l1-flatten' more than 'are you good at recursion'. That is worth stating and is not 'permanently unusable for selection', which is what I said. Q88 is rewritten.
misconceptions.generalisable_lesson: Third session running where the finding came from checking a claim rather than writing code, and the first where the claim was mine. M43 was a criterion nobody had checked; M45 was a board summary I quoted instead of the criteria; this is a sentence I authored, propagated through three documents, and never tested. A claim gets more durable each time it is repeated and none of those repetitions is evidence. The moment to check a claim is when you are about to build on it -- which is also the moment you are least inclined to, because it is load-bearing and checking it might cost you the plan.

decisions.decision: A drill targets only a confident tag
alternatives: Drill the weakest tag whatever the evidence behind it
decisions.rationale: Drilling on one observation acts on a single unlucky afternoon, which is what MIN_OBSERVATIONS exists to prevent. A tag the player has never met needs meeting, and that is the selection ordering's job.

alternatives: Pick a round number like 3 or 5 independently of the threshold
decisions.rationale: Tying them means the tag is confident again exactly when the drill ends, so the game never adapts to a drill whose result it cannot yet measure. The one number in this waypoint that is derived rather than guessed.

decisions.decision: Drills are injected after a clear, not put behind a command
decisions.rationale: A command is a thing nobody runs. After a clear is when the player is already asking what comes next, which is what the design means by injection.

decisions.decision: A multi-level tag cycles its levels; a single-level tag repeats and reports it
alternatives: Always repeat the first matching level
decisions.rationale: Three runs of one level drills the level rather than the skill. Where the content cannot offer variety, distinct_levels makes the thinness visible instead of implying a breadth that is not there.

decisions.decision: choose_drill returns None rather than an empty drill
alternatives: An always-present Drill with a possibly-empty queue
decisions.rationale: 'No drill' is the common case and the caller phrases it differently anyway. An empty queue is a shape that invites being rendered as though it were a drill.
